_comment: Guest-screen coordinates for the 1024x768 Mac OS 9 screen.
Regions are [x, y, width, height] in guest pixels; points are [x, y].
Derivation (all layout is computed at runtime from qd.screenBits in a
1024x768 guest, so these values are stable):
Splash window (src/ui/splash_window.c): width = 1024*3/4 = 768,
y = (768-576)/2 = 96. documentProc content starts 1 px inside the left
edge and 20 px below the top (title bar): content origin (129,116),
portRect about 766x555. The Start Game button is
((right-120)/2, 190, (right+120)/2, 215) in port coordinates, i.e. about
x 323..443, y 190..215, so on the guest screen it is x 452..572,
y 306..331; the point below is its centre.
Game window (src/ui/game_window.c): width = 1024*4/5 = 819,
documentProc content origin is (103,60); portRect is about 817x667.
sBlockSelectorRect.top = 667-40-10 = 617; sDisplayRect is
(10,10,807,607) in port coordinates, i.e. (113,70,910,667) on the guest
screen (797x597). The camera is set so Iso_Project(24,24,0) lands at
(displayWidth/2, displayHeight/2) = (398,298) display-local ->
(408,308) port-local -> (511,368) on the guest screen. That is the top
of the centre block of the 12x12 plateau, so the 'tile' point is the
diamond centre and 'tile' is a box around that diamond plus its two
faces (32x16 top face, faces to 16 px below).
'outside-tile' is a fixed patch in the upper-left of the display that a
single placed/removed block at the centre can never touch.
If game_window.c or splash_window.c change the window size or display
rect, re-derive these numbers; nothing else in the harness hard-codes
window geometry.
